newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE says Belgrade must accept opposition win.
newsitem.headline: OSCE says Belgrade must accept opposition win.

text.p: Europe's top security body called on Belgrade on Thursday to give full recognition of opposition victories in Serbia's controversial November 17 municipal poll.

"Step-by-step concessions to opposition on what ought to be a merely mechanical issue -- translating the results into seats -- is simply not the way to handle this situation," said Niels Helveg Petersen, Danish foreign minister and chairman-in-office of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation (OSCE).

Two weeks ago, the Vienna-based OSCE backed a report by former Spanish premier Felipe Gonzalez on the disputed local poll and said Belgrade should fully and promptly implement all its recommendations.
"The situation in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (FRY) is a fast evolving one. On one point it has, however, not been fast enough," Petersen told the OSCE's permanent council in a speech.

"The Gonzalez report stressed the need for immediate and complete implementation of the November election results. The Permanent Council at its first session this year endorsed this conclusion," he added.
The chairman added that the OSCE remained open for dialogue with the Serbian government of President Slobodan Milosevic to help resolve the "profound political crisis" in the country.
"Our door is wide open. But the FRY does not seem to want to walk through it," Petersen said.

He added that without full democratisation there was no chance of resolving the situation in Serbia, which has seen eight weeks of mass protests against the annulment of election wins by the Zajedno (Together) coalition of opposition parties in 14 of Serbia's 18 biggest cities.
Election commissions in the capital Belgrade and the country's second biggest city Nis earlier this week awarded victory in the polls to Zajedno.
